findings.location: get_remote_address keying + Limiter construction vs the shipped frontend-proxy topology
findings.finding: Rate limiting is keyed to the direct TCP peer (request.client.host; uvicorn runs without --proxy-headers and no code reads X-Forwarded-For) and stored per-process in memory. In the shipped deployment the Next.js server rewrites /api/* server-side to the backend, so every end user of one frontend instance shares one bucket: 200/min default and 10/min on login. The UI is poll-heavy per open tab (NavBar badge 5s = 12 req/min on every page; task detail 4 parallel polls at 3-5s ≈ 57 req/min), so ~3 concurrent users with a task page open collectively exceed the shared 200/min default — producing real, intermittent 429s, while direct hits to the exposed backend port (8000 in compose) bypass per-IP throttling unevenly.
findings.evidence: Installed slowapi util.py:20-27 (get_remote_address returns request.client.host); next.config.mjs:58-65 rewrites /api/* server-side; compose sets NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://backend:8000; polling arithmetic from the UI survey (NavBar 5s, tasks list 4s, task detail 3/4/5/5s, epics 5s, approvals 5s); limits configurable at config.py:2126-2145 (defaults+topology mismatch, not a hardcoded dead end).
findings.production_impact: Availability for teams beyond ~2-3 simultaneously active users through the bundled proxy (false 429s), and uneven brute-force protection when clients can reach the backend directly. Single-user/self-hosted/direct-API deployments are unaffected.
findings.confidence: High (code-verified; not load-tested through the proxy)
findings.recommendation: Any one closes it: key by authenticated user (jwt sub, falling back to IP); or trust/parse X-Forwarded-For behind a documented trusted proxy AND have the Next proxy forward it; and/or raise RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULT for the proxied deployment with the arithmetic documented in docs/DEPLOYMENT.md.

findings.location: Limiter construction — no storage_uri, so slowapi uses per-process in-memory storage
findings.finding: The Limiter is constructed without storage_uri (slowapi default in-memory), so effective limits multiply N× across uvicorn workers/replicas — e.g. the 10/min login cap becomes 20/min with two workers. There is no config knob for a Redis-backed limiter even though Redis is already a first-class dependency (RQ/streams). Latent today (single replica), silent the moment a second replica is added.
findings.evidence: rate_limit.py:25-29 (no storage_uri argument); no rate-limit storage field in config.py; compose/CI never run multiple backend replicas today.
findings.production_impact: None at single-replica scale; the control degrades silently (limits multiply) as soon as a second replica or worker is added.
findings.recommendation: Add an optional RATE_LIMIT_STORAGE_URI setting passed to Limiter(storage_uri=...) (slowapi supports redis:// natively), defaulted unset to preserve current behavior.

findings.location: 429 responses deviate from the app-wide {error:{code,message}} contract; UI degrades to a generic message
findings.finding: main.py registers slowapi's built-in _rate_limit_exceeded_handler, which returns {"error": "Rate limit exceeded: <limit>"} — error is a string, not the object every other handler produces. The frontend's fallback reads body.error.message, which is undefined for a string, so the user sees 'Request failed: 429' instead of the real reason. Cosmetic/UX only — throttling still works.
findings.evidence: slowapi 0.1.10 extension.py:76-87 (verified in the installed package); main.py:1870 registration; apps/web/lib/api.ts:28-38 fallback chain.
findings.production_impact: Operators and users lose the self-explanatory throttling message at exactly the moment they need it; no functional effect.
findings.recommendation: Replace the registered handler with a 3-line wrapper emitting {"error":{"code":"429","message": str(exc.detail)}} (keeping slowapi's header injection via limiter._inject_headers).
